mistakes.note: Known NPC summary says Vane is hunting whoever slits caravans' waterskins; the PC was never told his mission.

Narrator opened a Loose End that Tamsin carries something in her saddle a Border Guard captain must not search, which the PC never saw; it then reached Choices in rounds 15, 26 and 27 and was picked at M59.
Loose End states Vane means to arrest Tamsin at the Well of Ashar tomorrow, a hidden plan nobody told the PC; repeated in a round 26 Loose End and Choices in rounds 20 and 28.
Sefa, a hired rider, names her captain and the Kesh paymaster on first asking, with nothing offered.
Looks recorded for Captain Hask, who never appears on the page, and a portrait drawn of him.
The trough, cut at the base of the tallest spire, is now at the camp shelf a mile east of the spires (Vane waters the bay at it, Tamsin warns of the gap by it).
The hobble is 'still on' the grey, though at M80 it slithered off her fetlock into the sand.
The grey bolted with 'no water on her' (M80, and a Known fact), yet comes back dragging a full camp skin.
Vane and Tamsin plan the next leg straight onto the Glass Flats, skipping the Well of Ashar that lies between and that everyone meant to reach; a round 45 Choice repeats it.
The packs go on again and the grey is placed between the quiet camels again, both already done at M88-M90.
World Change fact says the sandstorm will reach the road within two days while the page has its wall on them and the grey already lost in it; the wall fact was retired instead of reconciled.
NPC knows repeated: Governor Hale given two near-identical lines about being short of money and trusting Marrick.
Carrying drops the full waterskin Wren tied to the bay and adds a 'spare waterskin', and keeps the spare blanket.

Loose Ends left open after the page answered them: Sefa's offer until dark (dark came and went), Sefa will burn the letters (she rode off), and the pistol lying on the blanket after Vane belted it at M68.
Ossery's and the Free Wells' Plot Thread nows never moved after round 2, still saying 'tomorrow night' and 'three nights from now' on day 3; Vane's thread still says arrest 'tomorrow'.
The World Bible never grew: no entry for Hask, the riders' hollow and burnt guild letters, or the camp shelf.
Jory's portrait is a bare-chested adult man with short brown hair, from a garbled prompt that never describes him.
Vane's portrait shows a linen tunic and indigo caftan, not his dusty blue officer's coat with brass buttons.
Vane stands beside his horse, though the narration has him mounted with sabre drawn.
Wren is missing from the picture and Jory wears her straw hat.
Wren barefoot rather than in riding boots, and the waterskins drawn as metal jugs.
Mud-brick walls and towers invented at a bare stone shelf in the desert, recurring in the M86 and M90 pictures.

choices.reason: Three distinct, fitting options most rounds and picks steer the parley, but two secrets reach Choices (saddle, arrest) and the storm stretch offers near-twins of hobble, load or watch.

surprise.reason: The riders' cache with burnt Lell guild letters and Sefa's unseen captain land well, but Ossery's sabotage and the Free Wells never surface and the storm came from the bench.

threads.reason: Only the dust-riders' thread moves (Sefa to Hask, a new strike planned); Ossery's and the Free Wells' threads sit unchanged for 43 rounds and the caravan never reaches Ashar.

characters.reason: Vane, Tamsin and Jory each have a voice and want, and keep to it; Sefa giving up her employer on first asking is the notable lapse.

continuity.reason: Small slips a careful reader catches: the trough moving a mile to camp, the hobble and dry camel at M84, the Flats talked of as the next leg, packs loaded twice.

pacing.reason: Eleven rounds of one standoff with repeated beats (sabre levelled, thumb in belt) and twelve of camel-handling around the storm; 45 rounds cover under a day and never leave the first camp.

prose.reason: Spare, physical, consistent voice with good dialogue; tics (thumb along the sabre guard, good hand, spitting) and one garbled word at M6.

pictures.reason: Scenes mostly show the moment with the right people, but Jory's portrait is the wrong person entirely, Vane's portrait drops his uniform, and Wren goes missing at M31.

secrets.reason: Loose Ends hand the player Tamsin's hidden saddle cargo and Vane's arrest plan, echoed in Choices, and the opening Journal gives away Vane's mission.

agency.reason: Moves carried out as given with no added lines or feelings for Wren; the Narrator only corrects premises (Vane not walking the horses).

stakes.reason: Failures bite (bolt into the grey, the grey bolting into the storm, Sefa riding off) and the storm ride is checked, but many Checks fall on plain talk, and the split skin is soon refunded.

state.reason: Many stale or wrong records: Loose Ends leaking secrets and never retired, two threads frozen, lore never growing, carried items and the World Change fact out of step with the page.

adventure.reason: The ambush at the Red Teeth and the ride into the sandstorm are met on the page and won by the PC's own moves, but the road never advances past the first camp and the well, Flats and set pieces ahead stay talk.

violence.reason: A crossbow bolt into a camel's neck and a wrenched shoulder, brief and soon past.
